Technology stocks were falling in recent trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 dropping almost 2.3% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was posting a nearly 1.9% decrease.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Arista Networks ( ANET ) was 6% higher retracing half of a nearly 12% advance earlier in Friday's session that followed the cloud networking company reporting improved Q3 financial results and beating Wall Street expectations, prompting RBC Capital Markets to increase its price target for the company's stock by $10 to $300 a share.
In other sector news:
VeriSign ( VRSN ) soared to its best share price since the height of the internet boom in September 2000, rising over 25% to $176.59 a share after the domain name registry company reported Q3 net income of $1.23 per share, up from $1.00 per share during the year-ago period and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.04 per share. The company also disclosed it reached a deal with the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers to raise prices for ".com" names.
(-) Apple ( AAPL ) slumped badly Friday, recently falling more than 7%, after CFO Luca Maestri said during a conference call late Thursday that the technology giant will no longer provide iPhone unit sales data starting with results for the current quarter ending Dec. 31. The announcement upstaged better-than-expected fiscal Q4 financial results, earning $2.91 per share on $62.9 billion in sales compared with the Street view expecting $2.78 per share on $61.6 billion in sales. iPhone sales were little changed from year-ago levels at 46.9 million compared with 46.7 million.
